examples.en: We play rock, paper, scissors to bet on lunch.
I lost at rock, paper, scissors, so I will go first.
The kids are playing rock, paper, scissors.

examples.ko: 가위바위보 해서 이긴 사람이 먼저 골라요!
examples.en: The winner of rock, paper, scissors picks first!

examples.ko: 가위바위보를 세 번 했는데 계속 비겼어요.
examples.en: We played rock, paper, scissors three times and kept tying.
Shall we do rock, paper, scissors to decide who goes first?

explain: 순서나 당번을 빨리 정할 때 한국 사람들이 자주 해요. 동사는 '하다'를 써서 '가위바위보를 하다'라고 해요. 이기면 '이기다', 지면 '지다', 같으면 '비기다'라고 하고, 시작할 때는 다 같이 '가위바위보!' 하고 외쳐요.

phrases.en: Let's play rock, paper, scissors to see who goes first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임을 한다고 말할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic way to say you play the game.

phrases.en: I'm happy because I won at rock, paper, scissors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 말할 때 '이기다/지다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach 이기다/지다 to talk about the result.

phrases.en: We decide the cleaning duty by rock, paper, scissors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순서나 당번을 빨리 정할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to quickly decide an order or duty.

explain_en: Koreans use it all the time to settle turns or chores quickly. The verb is '하다': '가위바위보를 하다'. Then '이기다' (win), '지다' (lose), '비기다' (tie). Players shout '가위바위보!' together to start.

examples.ko: 아버지가 생일에 야구 글러브를 사 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father bought me a baseball glove for my birthday.
The glove is so big that my hand feels loose in it.
I put on boxing gloves and hit the punching bag.
I wrote my name on the glove.
Gloves for left-handed players are sold separately.
The ball slipped neatly into the glove.

explain: 겨울에 끼는 손 장갑은 '장갑'이라고 하고, 글러브는 야구나 복싱처럼 운동할 때 끼는 것을 말할 때 써요. 영어 'glove'는 둘 다 가리키지만 한국어는 나눠서 말해요.

phrases.en: I put on a baseball glove and caught the ball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구에서 쓰는 글러브예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The glove used in baseball.

phrases.en: Boxing gloves are heavier than I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복싱에서 쓰는 글러브예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The glove used in boxing.

phrases.en: I put on my glove and started practicing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손에 착용할 때 '끼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'put on' for wearing it on the hand.

explain_en: The winter hand glove is called '장갑', while 글러브 is used for gloves worn in sports like baseball and boxing. English 'glove' covers both, but Korean separates them.

examples.en: The squad arrived at the airport yesterday.
The Olympic delegation totals two hundred people.
Fans gave the squad a big round of applause.
The team bus stopped in front of the stadium.
The coach gathered the squad and explained the plan.
Let's sing our team's cheer song together.

explain: 선수들뿐 아니라 감독, 코치, 스태프까지 포함한 팀 전체를 가리킬 때 써요. 선수 개인은 '선수', 한 경기에 나가는 팀은 '팀'이라고 해요. 국가대표나 구단 단위의 큰 무리를 말할 때 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The manager led the team into the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감독이나 단장처럼 팀 전체를 책임지는 사람 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used about a manager or head who is in charge of the whole team.

phrases.en: The Korean delegation won a gold medal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라 이름 앞에 붙여 국가대표 팀 전체를 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a country name in front to refer to a whole national team naturally.

phrases.en: The whole squad took a photo together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선수뿐 아니라 감독과 스태프까지 모두 함께라는 뜻을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes that everyone, including the coach and staff, is included.

explain_en: The whole body of a sports team, including players, coaches, and staff. An individual is a '선수' and a team that plays in one game is a '팀'. It sounds natural for national squads or club-level groups.

dis.h: all players and staff of a club

p.n: 팀 is more general and does not stress the whole squad with staff.

t90.ax: Let's sing our team's cheer song together.

examples.en: Our team wins the final.
Korea won yesterday's match.

examples.ko: 끝까지 포기하지 않아서 승리할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: We could win because we did not give up until the end.
The players who won waved their hands.
If we win this time too, we are champions.

examples.ko: 마지막 경기에서 승리하고 나서 모두 울었어요.
examples.en: After winning the last match, everyone cried.

explain: '이기다'가 일상에서 더 흔하고, '승리하다'는 경기나 선거, 전쟁 같은 큰 일에 쓰는 글말 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '패배하다'이고, '지다'가 일상 반대말이에요.

phrases.en: Our team won yesterday's game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: Our team won a big victory.
phrases.nuance_ko: '승리하다'보다 더 격식 있는 말로, 결과를 얻었다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal phrase that stresses having achieved the victory.

phrases.en: They give a prize to the winning team.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 명사 앞에서 이긴 사람이나 팀을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe who won.

explain_en: '이기다' is more common in daily talk, while '승리하다' has a written feel and suits big events such as matches, elections and wars. Its opposite is '패배하다', and the everyday opposite is '지다'.

examples.ko: 전반전에 우리 팀이 한 골 넣었어요.
examples.en: Our team scored one goal in the first half.
The first half is over and it's halftime.
It rained heavily throughout the first half.
A player was hurt during the first half and was substituted.
The first half ended 0 to 0.
I ate dinner after watching the first half.

explain: 전반전은 축구나 농구 같은 경기의 앞쪽 절반이고, 뒤쪽 절반은 '후반전'이에요. 줄여서 '전반', '후반'이라고도 많이 해요. 둘 사이에 쉬는 시간은 '하프타임'이라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 전반에 우리 팀이 두 골을 넣었어요.
phrases.en: Our team scored two goals in the first half.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전반전'을 줄인 말로, 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 전반전, often used in speech.

phrases.en: We won in the second half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전반전의 짝말이고, 경기의 뒤쪽 절반을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 전반전; the second half of a game.

phrases.en: I drink water at halftime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전반전과 후반전 사이의 쉬는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The break between the first and second halves.

explain_en: 전반전 is the first half of a game such as soccer or basketball, and the second half is '후반전'. People often shorten them to '전반' and '후반'. The break between them is called '하프타임'.

examples.en: The athlete lightly jumped over the high hurdle.
Rhythm is important in hurdle races.
I tripped on a hurdle during PE class.
The hurdle to getting a job feels too high.
Passing the exam is the first hurdle.
Try clearing the small hurdles one by one first.

explain: 육상 경기 말고도 '입학 허들', '진입 허들'처럼 넘기 어려운 조건이나 장벽을 비유로 말할 때 써요. 이럴 때는 '허들이 높다/낮다', '허들을 넘다'처럼 말해요. 영어 hurdle에서 온 외래어예요.

phrases.en: I got over the first hurdle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 조건이나 단계를 통과했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you pass a difficult condition or stage.

phrases.en: The bar to get into this company is high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어가기 어렵다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is hard to get in.

phrases.en: The barrier to start this class is low.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉽게 시작할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is easy to get started.

explain_en: Beyond track and field, it is used figuratively for a hard condition or barrier, as in '입학 허들' or '진입 허들'. In that sense say '허들이 높다/낮다' or '허들을 넘다'. It is a loanword from English 'hurdle'.

examples.en: I jumped from the plane wearing a parachute.
Once the parachute opened, I began to come down slowly.
I attached a parachute to the box and dropped it.
The rescue team sent supplies down by parachute.
Parachute training is very dangerous.
The kids played a parachute game on the playground.

explain: 비행기에서 뛰어내릴 때 쓰는 도구예요. 한국어에서는 여기서 나온 '낙하산 인사'라는 말이 더 자주 들려요. 실력이 아니라 연줄로 높은 자리에 오른 사람을 부정적으로 말할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 새 사장이 낙하산 인사라서 직원들이 불만이 많아요.
phrases.en: an appointment by connections
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력이 아닌 연줄로 높은 자리에 간 사람을 비판할 때 써요. 대부분 부정적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically for someone placed in a high position through connections rather than merit. It is almost always negative.

explain_en: It is the equipment used when jumping from an airplane. In Korean, the derived phrase '낙하산 인사' is heard even more often, a negative term for someone placed in a high post through connections rather than ability.

examples.en: Grandfather cuts the grass with a sickle.
A sickle has a sharp blade, so you must be careful.

examples.ko: 농사를 짓는 분들은 낫을 자주 써요.
examples.en: People who farm often use sickles.
A sickle hangs in the storage shed of the country house.
I bought a new sickle.

examples.ko: 벼를 낫으로 베던 시절 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about the days when rice was cut with sickles.

explain: 풀이나 곡식을 베는, 끝이 굽은 농기구예요. 소리가 같은 '낫다'(병이 나아지다, 더 좋다)와 헷갈리지 않게 문장 속 쓰임을 봐야 해요. 낫은 '낫이, 낫을, 낫으로'처럼 받침 ㅅ이 다음 소리로 넘어가요.

phrases.en: Grandfather cuts the rice with a sickle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'로 도구를 나타내는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic usage, with 으로 marking the tool.

phrases.en: I sharpen the sickle before working.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날을 세울 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for sharpening the blade.

phrases.en: The new sickle is very sharp.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낫이'처럼 받침 ㅅ이 다음 소리로 넘어가는 형태를 익히세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Note how the final ㅅ carries over into the next sound in 낫이.

explain_en: It's the farm tool with a curved blade for cutting grass or grain. Don't confuse it with the verb 낫다 (to get better, to be better), which sounds the same; context tells them apart. With particles the ㅅ carries over, as in 낫이, 낫을, 낫으로.

examples.en: The bike had rusted, so I wiped it.

examples.ko: 비를 맞은 못에 녹이 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A lot of rust formed on the nails that got rained on.
If you spray rust remover, it comes off easily.
The old key was covered in rust.

examples.ko: 칼에 녹이 슬지 않게 물기를 닦아 두세요.
examples.en: Wipe off the moisture so the knife doesn't rust.

examples.ko: 다리 난간에 붉은 녹이 올라와 있었어요.
examples.en: Red rust had come up on the bridge railing.

explain: '녹이 슬다'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. 쇠가 녹는다는 뜻의 '녹다'와 소리가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요. 쇠로 된 물건에만 쓰고, 오래 안 써서 둔해진 걸 '녹슬다'로도 말해요.

phrases.en: I repainted the rusty bicycle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '녹슨'은 녹이 슨 물건을 꾸며 주는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 녹슨 describes an object that has rusted.

phrases.en: I wiped the rust off the knife.
phrases.nuance_ko: 녹을 없앨 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for removing rust.

phrases.en: The key I left for a long time rusted.
phrases.nuance_ko: '녹'에서 나온 동사로, 쇠가 녹이 생기는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb made from 녹, meaning metal gets rusty.

explain_en: The natural pairing is '녹이 슬다'. It sounds like the verb '녹다' (to melt) but is a different word. It's for metal things, and '녹슬다' is also used for skills that have gone dull from lack of use.

examples.en: Grandfather reads the newspaper wearing reading glasses.

examples.ko: 돋보기로 보면 곤충의 날개가 자세히 보여요.
examples.en: With a magnifying glass, you can see an insect's wings in detail.
My eyesight got worse, so I started to need reading glasses.
The researcher looked through a magnifying glass all day.

examples.ko: 작은 글씨는 돋보기 없이 못 읽어요.
examples.en: I can't read small print without reading glasses.

examples.ko: 돋보기 앱을 켜면 스마트폰으로 글씨를 키울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you open a magnifier app, you can enlarge text on your smartphone.

explain: 작은 것을 크게 보는 렌즈도 '돋보기'이고, 나이가 들어 가까운 글씨가 안 보일 때 쓰는 안경도 '돋보기'라고 해요. 안경을 분명히 말할 때는 '돋보기안경'이라고도 해요. 스마트폰의 확대 기능도 '돋보기'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I got new reading glasses made.
phrases.nuance_ko: 렌즈가 아니라 안경이라는 점을 분명히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear it's glasses, not a hand lens.

phrases.en: Hold a magnifying glass over the small text.
phrases.nuance_ko: 렌즈를 글씨나 물건 위에 가져다 대는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The action of holding the lens over text or an object.
phrases.en_equiv: to hold up a magnifying glass

phrases.example: 스마트폰 돋보기 기능으로 글씨를 크게 봤어요.
phrases.en: I enlarged the text with my phone's magnifier feature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰의 확대 기능을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a phone's zoom feature.

explain_en: A lens that enlarges small things is a '돋보기', and so are the glasses people wear when close-up text gets hard to see with age. To make clear it's glasses, people also say '돋보기안경'. The zoom feature on smartphones is called '돋보기' too.

t90.ax: I can't read small print without reading glasses.

examples.en: I read a book in front of the living room fireplace.
I put firewood in the fireplace.
I want to live in a house with a fireplace.

examples.ko: 눈 오는 날 벽난로 불빛이 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: The fireplace light looks warm on a snowy day.

examples.ko: 아이들이 벽난로 앞에 모여 이야기를 들어요.
examples.en: The kids gather in front of the fireplace and listen to a story.
Apartments these days almost never have a fireplace.

explain: 한국의 전통 집에는 온돌이 있어서 벽난로는 서양 영화나 펜션에서 더 자주 봐요. '벽난로에 불을 피우다', '벽난로 앞에 앉다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: On the cold night, I lit a fire in the fireplace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벽난로를 사용하는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for using a fireplace.
phrases.en_equiv: to light a fire in the fireplace

phrases.en: The family sat in front of the fireplace and talked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따뜻하고 편안한 분위기를 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a warm, cozy atmosphere.

phrases.example: 저는 벽난로가 있는 집에서 살고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to live in a house with a fireplace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집의 특징을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a feature of a house.

explain_en: Traditional Korean houses have ondol floor heating, so fireplaces are more often seen in Western movies or pensions. You say '벽난로에 불을 피우다' and '벽난로 앞에 앉다'.

examples.ko: 태풍 뒤에 마을 사람들이 길을 복구했어요.
examples.en: After the typhoon the villagers restored the road.
I want to recover the file I deleted.
The technician restored the internet quickly for me.

examples.ko: 다리를 복구하는 데 일 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a year to repair the bridge.
I'm glad the restored photo looks just like before.
To recover data, first look for the backup.

explain: 고장 나거나 부서진 것을 원래 상태로 되돌리는 일에 써요. 컴퓨터 파일, 도로, 전기처럼 큰 피해를 고칠 때 많이 말해요. 작은 물건을 고치는 일에는 '고치다'를 써요. '복원하다'는 옛 모습을 되살리는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 비가 그친 뒤에 마을에서 복구 작업을 시작했어요.
phrases.en: After the rain stopped, the village started the recovery work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재난이나 사고 뒤에 원래대로 고치는 일을 '복구 작업'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fixing things back to normal after a disaster or accident is called '복구 작업'.

phrases.en: The technicians restored the power overnight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끊긴 전기, 물, 인터넷 같은 서비스를 다시 쓰게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for getting a cut-off service like power, water, or internet working again.

phrases.en: Please recover the photos I deleted by mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터나 휴대폰 자료를 되살려 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to get back data on a computer or phone.

explain_en: It is for bringing something broken or damaged back to its original state, often for big damage such as computer files, roads, or power. For small objects use 고치다. 복원하다 feels like reviving an old appearance.

t90.ax: It took a year to repair the bridge.

examples.en: A small bird is singing inside the birdcage.

examples.ko: 새장 문을 열어 두었더니 새가 날아갔어요.
examples.en: I left the birdcage door open and the bird flew away.
I hung the birdcage by the sunny window.

examples.ko: 아이가 새장에 모이를 넣어 주고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is putting feed into the birdcage.

examples.ko: 새장이 너무 작아서 새가 불편해 보여요.
examples.en: The birdcage is so small that the bird looks uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 새장 청소는 일주일에 한 번 해요.
examples.en: I clean the birdcage once a week.

explain: '새장'은 사람이 새를 기르려고 가두는 곳이라, 새가 직접 짓는 '둥지'나 새를 위해 달아 주는 '새집'과 달라요. '새장 속의 새'처럼 자유가 없는 처지를 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The bird in the cage looks out the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새장에 있는 새를 말하고, 자유가 없는 처지를 비유하기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a caged bird and can also mean someone without freedom.

phrases.example: 새가 새장에 갇혀서 날 수 없어요.
phrases.en: The bird is locked in the cage and cannot fly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새가 나가지 못하는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a bird that cannot get out.
phrases.en_equiv: to be trapped in a cage

phrases.en: I clean the birdcage every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새를 기르는 사람이 자주 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A chore people who keep birds do often.

explain_en: A '새장' is where people keep a bird, unlike a '둥지' (nest) that birds build or a '새집' (birdhouse) put up for them. A phrase like '새장 속의 새' figuratively describes someone without freedom.

t90.ax: I clean the birdcage once a week.
